clue.text: Aim to include bull-ring and surroundings

definitions.meaning: an aim is the goal or object one shoots for
the archery board that has a bull's-eye at its centre, rings round it and an outer surround

explanation.surface: An instruction to take in a bullring and the area around it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bull-ring' is not the arena for bullfighting: read it as the bull and the rings of an archery or darts board.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are the thing aimed at: the purpose one has in view and the painted board with bull and circles.

clue.text: Paraded about in support

indicators.note: in puts the about word inside the support word

parts.note: aid means help or support
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Marchers paraded around in a show of support.
explanation.definitionFit: To show off views or clothes in public, putting them on display.

clue.text: Go-betweens ' as confidants

parts.note: the uprights a gate hangs between, and the third party in the phrase 'between you, me and the' one of them, used of a secret

explanation.surface: Intermediaries trusted with secrets.
explanation.walkthrough: A gate swings between two of these; the British saying 'between you and me and the gatepost' introduces something confidential.
explanation.definitionFit: The upright posts flanking a gate stand between, and the idiom makes one a silent sharer of secrets.

clue.text: Mouth organ? — Learner is not up to it

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards, backwards

parts.note: L is the learner symbol, as on British L-plates

explanation.surface: A beginner on the harmonica is not good enough to play it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mouth organ' is not a harmonica but an organ of the body in the mouth; 'to it' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the two lumps of tissue at the back of the throat, literally an organ in the mouth.

clue.text: -Clue — a' rip reformed, sui generis

indicators.note: reformed says the letters of these words are formed again in a new order

explanation.surface: A crossword clue torn up and rebuilt turns out to be one of a kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Sui generis is Latin for 'of its own kind', so unique or unusual, which is what odd or singular means.

clue.text: Abnormally, partly true — learn from it

indicators.note: from it says the answer is made out of the preceding letters, rearranged

explanation.surface: A strange statement, only half true, that one should learn something from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abnormally' is the definition, though it also hints at the scrambling; 'from it' tells you to build the answer from PARTLYTRUELEARN.
explanation.definitionFit: Beyond what is natural or normal, so in a way outside the ordinary course of things.

clue.text: Co-defendant in a — shooting gallery?

parts.note: read whole, it is an armoured chamber in a fort from which guns are fired

explanation.surface: Someone tried alongside another person for an incident at a fairground rifle range.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as CASE-MATE for a fellow defendant; a casemate is a vaulted gun chamber in a fortress wall, a gallery for shooting.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortified vault through whose openings guns fire, punningly a partner in a lawsuit.

clue.text: King holds- Victoria's title to be ghastly

indicators.note: holds means the king's name contains the letters of the title

parts.note: Lud is a legendary king of Britain, remembered in Ludgate
Victoria signed as Regina et Imperatrix, Queen and Empress, abbreviated R I

explanation.surface: A monarch keeps Queen Victoria's style and looks dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: King LUD is a legendary British ruler said to have founded London's Ludgate; R I stands for Regina Imperatrix.
explanation.definitionFit: Horrifying and sensational, like a gruesome tale, so shocking and ghastly.

clue.text: Essential people — one has met so few!

definitions.text: Essential people — one has met so few!

parts.words: Essential people — one has met so few!
parts.note: those without whom one would not exist, of whom a person meets only parents and grandparents

explanation.surface: Indispensable people, and yet you have encountered hardly any of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essential' means needed for one's existence: forebears.
explanation.definitionFit: Forebears are needed for anyone to be born, yet most lived long before.

clue.text: Advance offers to actors

definitions.meaning: people who put on a false show, feigning what they are not

explanation.surface: Early bids are made to members of a cast.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as PRE-TENDERS for the first sense: offers made in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors feign characters, and those who feign are pretenders; tenders are formal offers, so pre-tenders are offers made in advance.

clue.text: Shake foundation of church

definitions.meaning: to sway or make something sway violently
in Matthew's Gospel, Peter is the stone upon which Christ builds his church

explanation.surface: An earthquake or vandal shakes the base of a church building.
explanation.definitionFit: To sway something is to make it totter; Peter's name means stone, the base on which the church was to be built.

clue.text: Fitting in a joint that can be adjusted

indicators.note: in places the word for fitting inside the word for a joint

parts.note: a dive is a seedy bar or club, a low joint
fitting means apt, suitable

explanation.surface: A plumber fits a pipe into a joint that can be tightened or loosened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' looks like plumbing but is slang for a disreputable bar: DIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flexible and able to change to suit new conditions can be adjusted.

clue.text: Femme fatale amused herself perversely

indicators.note: perversely suggests the letters are twisted out of their proper order

explanation.surface: A seductress entertained herself in a wicked way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'herself' is a link word, keeping the surface about one woman.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Gorgon whose gaze turned men to stone, a deadly woman whose looks destroy those who see her.

clue.text: Clever fish ?

parts.note: fish that are experts, since a dab hand is a skilled person and the flatfish of that name come in plural

explanation.surface: A question about an intelligent fish.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'dab' is British for an expert (a 'dab hand'); dabs are also small flatfish. The question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Small flatfish share their name with skilled experts, so experts who are fish fit both readings.

clue.text: A strip, about ; completed — it's licentious

indicators.note: about means the strip word goes around the completed word

parts.note: a band is a strip of material
done means completed, finished

explanation.surface: A stripper performs about the place; once finished, the act is lewd.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild and dissolute, having given up all restraint, as in abandoned behaviour.

clue.text: Symbolism of part of Bible divides people

indicators.note: divides means the Bible part splits the people word in two, sitting inside it

parts.note: a nation is a people
OT is the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A section of scripture splits a community.
explanation.definitionFit: A system of written signs, as in music or chess, is a kind of symbolism.

clue.text: From agitator to royal adviser

parts.note: R stands for royal, as in RN or RA
a mentor is a trusted adviser

explanation.surface: A move from troublemaking to counselling the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' is a link word; the definition is 'agitator'.
explanation.definitionFit: One who agitates and harasses another, giving pain or distress.

clue.text: Below chop there's' part of a sirloin

parts.note: under means below
a cut is a chop

explanation.surface: Beneath the chop on the butcher's counter is a piece of the sirloin.
explanation.definitionFit: The undercut is the tenderloin, the tender underside of a sirloin of beef.

clue.text: Pram — very low one, after necessary reduction

parts.note: bass is the lowest range of voice or pitch
I is the Roman numeral for one
net is what remains once deductions such as tax are taken off

explanation.surface: A pram set very low to the ground once it has been suitably cut down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after necessary reduction' is not a position indicator: it defines NET, as in net pay.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooded wicker cradle or baby carriage, an old word for a pram.

clue.text: Censure about second scrape

indicators.note: about tells us the censure word goes round the abbreviation for second

parts.note: a rap is a rebuke, as in a rap on the knuckles

explanation.surface: Criticism over a brief scrape or minor scratch.
explanation.definitionFit: To rasp is to rub with a coarse file, grating a surface.

clue.text: Like tea, so to speak, it's sweet

definitions.meaning: the letter named 'tea', T, comes after the letter S in the alphabet
the pudding course of a meal, a dessert

explanation.surface: Tea is like something; so to put it, it is sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as AFTER S: the letter that sounds like 'tea' follows S. AFTERS is British slang for pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Following S is where T sits; and the course eaten after the main dish is dessert.

clue.text: Judge very fair for many in a calamitous case

indicators.note: in places the many letter inside the calamitous word
case means the calamitous word is a casing round the letter for many

parts.note: dire means dreadful, calamitous
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many

explanation.surface: A judge rules favourably on behalf of many people in a disastrous lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judge very fair' is the definition: to rate something very favourably. 'Case' is not a lawsuit but the container signal round M.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold in high regard is to think something excellent, rating it very highly.

clue.text: Urge Prime Minister, garlanded, to rise'

annotationWithheld.why: Urge Prime Minister, garlanded, to rise: IMPEL is LEI round PM reversed, but 'garlanded' must both give LEI and signal the containment, one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Urge Prime Minister, garlanded, to rise'

clue.text: Thinks of shows in reverse

definitions.meaning: gives back a mirror image, as glass does

explanation.surface: Someone muses over programmes broadcast backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To ponder something is to turn it over in the mind; a mirror throws back an image left to right.

clue.text: Prickly old character — Trollopean doctor, say

indicators.note: say tells us the doctor's name is pronounced, with the spelling changed

parts.note: Doctor Thorne is the title character of Anthony Trollope's novel

explanation.surface: A spiky elderly figure, a physician out of Trollope perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition works two ways: a thorn is prickly, and also an old runic letter (þ) used in Old English.
explanation.definitionFit: A spine on a rose is prickly, and the runic letter þ is an obsolete character of the alphabet.

clue.text: It's only a game ? Dash!

definitions.meaning: a children's card game in which matching cards are called out
a mild exclamation of annoyance, like 'blast!'

explanation.surface: A player tells himself it is only a game, then curses.
explanation.walkthrough: SNAP is a simple British card game; 'Snap!' was also said as a mild oath.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple card game where players shout when two cards match, and the same word as a sharp exclamation of irritation.

clue.text: Works together in group for singular sort of exam

definitions.meaning: a set of works, such as paintings or stamps, assembled together
..., plural, are the college examinations held at the start of term at Oxford

explanation.surface: People cooperate in a team ahead of a strange kind of test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Works' is a noun here (artworks), not a verb. At Oxford, 'collections' are internal college exams; 'singular' asks for the word without its S.
explanation.definitionFit: An assembled set of works in a museum, and one of the term-start tests at Oxford colleges.

clue.text: Worship so dilatory after Reformation

indicators.note: Reformation is literally a forming again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Religious devotion became sluggish once the Protestant Reformation came.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital R makes 'Reformation' look historical; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Worship of an image or false god, or excessive adoration of anything.

clue.text: A lot of onions chewed by King (Henry)

definitions.meaning: onions plaited together by their stems are sold in a line
Hilaire Belloc's cautionary tale of Henry King, who chewed little bits of this and died

explanation.surface: A monarch called Henry munches a large quantity of onions.
explanation.walkthrough: In Belloc's comic poem, Henry King 'chewed little bits of String' and was 'early cut off in dreadful agonies'.
explanation.definitionFit: Onions are sold tied in a line, and Belloc's Henry King fatally chewed bits of twine.
